title: MAX_SPAN cap is correct for integrity but introduces a LIVENESS lag: if the loop wakes less often than the cap covers, the cursor can permanently trail real income (under-count, never over-count)
description: FIND-702 was correctly closed for INTEGRITY by capping the scan: MAX_SPAN=9000 (record-earn.mjs:121), to=min(now, cursor+MAX_SPAN) (122), and the cursor is advanced ONLY to `to` (125). This guarantees a single eth_getLogs never exceeds the provider range limit and the cursor never jumps past unscanned blocks. The side effect is a liveness gap: Base produces ~43,200 blocks/day (~2s/block), so if a wake processes only 9000 blocks and `now` advances by more than 9000 between wakes (i.e. the loop runs less often than roughly once per ~5 hours), the cursor falls further behind every run and never catches up — genuinely earned external USDC in the un-scanned tail is recorded late or, if `now` keeps outrunning the cap, effectively never. This is strictly an UNDER-count / monotonic / fail-safe behavior: it can NEVER fabricate or inflate a USDC number, so it does NOT fail the core integrity question or any review dimension. It is recorded as a non-blocking advisory only.
fix: Future increment (not a sprint-8 blocker): within a single wake, loop eth_getLogs in <=MAX_SPAN windows from cursor+1 up to `now`, summing external inflow and advancing the cursor per completed window, so a wide gap after downtime still fully settles in one run while each individual getLogs stays under the provider cap. Add a test feeding now-cursor > MAX_SPAN and asserting all windows are summed and the cursor reaches `now`.
